title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
authors: Andrew J. Ochoa, Martin J. A. Schuetz, Helmut G. Katzgraber
abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions. We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing. We validate our approach on a test bed of 43 problem instances from QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, achieving diversity amplification factors, defined as the increase in the number of distinct solutions at a given set size, of up to 11923x with a median of 24.3x across different problem scales and hardness parameters. Because exact ground-state degeneracies are known for these instances, the recovered fraction of the manifold can be measured rather than bounded: post-processing recovers a median of 21% of the ground-state manifold, and provably all of it for six instances. We also demonstrate that, in some cases, the classical post-processing can discover independent sets larger than those found by the quantum hardware, thus improving on solution quality and not just diversity. While the method is non-ergodic and cannot guarantee complete manifold coverage, it consistently discovers a larger number of high-quality, and in some cases strictly better, configurations than quantum sampling alone. This work demonstrates how simple classical post-processing can enhance the utility of quantum optimization results.
summary: This paper presents a hybrid method to enhance quantum optimization results for problems like MIS using Rydberg atom arrays. It combines initial solutions from quantum hardware with a classical post-processing technique called Houdayer cluster updates. This classical step dramatically increases the discovered solution diversity and can even find better solutions than the quantum hardware alone.
main_problem: The core problem is exploring and systematically amplifying the ground-state manifold of NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, such as Maximum Independent Set (MIS).
main_result: The hybrid quantum-classical approach achieved diversity amplification factors up to 11923x and recovered a median of 21% of the true ground-state manifold for tested instances.
method: A hybrid approach where quantum hardware provides initial solution seeds, which are then systematically expanded using a classical post-processing algorithm based on Houdayer cluster updates.
model_or_system: The physical platform utilized is Rydberg atom arrays, specifically demonstrated on QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, encoding the MIS problem on unit disk graphs.
key_observables: Solution Diversity Amplification Factor, Recovered Fraction of the Ground-State Manifold, and the size of the discovered independent set compared to the quantum hardware output.
important_parameters: The problem instances are drawn from a test bed of 43 instances, and the key mechanism relies on the structure of connected components (clusters) within the symmetric difference of two solutions.
main_assumptions: The method is fundamentally non-ergodic and cannot guarantee complete manifold coverage, and the quantum hardware is assumed to suffer from inherent sampling limitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Houdayer cluster update mechanism, detailing how exchanging entire connected components between two solutions generates multiple distinct candidates, and show the overall algorithm flow.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the MIS problem on Rydberg arrays, details the quantum sampling limitations, and then systematically applies the Houdayer cluster update algorithm in a classical post-processing step to expand the solution space, validating the results on multiple benchmark instances.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum hardware limitations (sampling bias) with classical algorithmic power, showing a concrete method to extract far more information from quantum measurements than the raw output suggests, which is highly relevant for interpreting quantum simulation results.
